name: LRoc
notes: A keyboardist's model, so the melody block is the model and everything else is context. The documented device is exact — "LRoc's keyboard vamp – of three notes, no less – sets it off" — so `motifPitchCount` is pinned at 3, `articulation` is staccato with `endVariation` false because "no sustain pedal — staccato repetition is the point", and the register is the C4–C6 the research gives rather than crunk's mid-keyboard stab. That high floor is also what keeps him off the 808: "the vamp is deliberately above the sub's register so both read on a club system", which is why `drums.bass808.register` drops to the bottom of the range and the melody starts at 60. ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set, and it is a description rather than an exemption: "no chords, just a motif that implies i". The chord part's variety therefore comes from how long the loop sits — a wide `chordDurationBeats`, three `harmonicRhythm` values and a wide voicing register — rather than from progressions he does not play. ⚠ The i–VI and i–VII families carry low weights and are INFERRED; the research names only the static form, and they are the first thing to delete if this ever sounds busier than the records. ⚠ The kit is Lil Jon's 808/909, and his own parts "are written to sit in the gaps between clap and kick" — so the kick here is authored one hit plainer than Lil Jon's own model and the hats a shade lighter, to leave those gaps open. Those drum numbers are INFERRED from that one sentence. ⚠ The hook's second line, "a third or sixth above", is approximated by a chord-tone `arp` counter at the melody's own octave; the engine's counter offsets by octaves, not by intervals. ⚠ `medium`, tracking the research's high-medium: the three-note vamp, the gear and one major credit are sourced; the tempo band is inherited from Lil Jon's lane. ⚠ `fills.snareRollLadder` is off — with both fill periods at 4 bars the big fill wins and the inherited ladder reads no seed, so it would write one identical fill on every seed. ⚠ `countermelody.registerOffset` moved from 0 to 12: inside a fifth the counter sits in the melody's own register and plays its pitches at the same moment, which `coherence.rs` calls a second lead rather than an answer. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 858 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 907/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ `countermelody.fillGapsOnly` returned to true. Its empty-bar bias was already negligible (0.02), so silence was not what bound this one: with fill-gaps off the counter plays THROUGH the lead rather than around it, and the two lines land on the same moments every seed. It waits its turn now.
